title: Concierge onramp: microflows + telemetry recipes (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This doc is an experimental playbook for a low-friction, concierge-style SDK onramp aimed at engineers who want to ship a first integration in 30 minutes. It focuses on tiny, testable microflows, explicit telemetry hooks, and short lab recipes that we can run with customers or internal advocates.

Audience:
- Platform/SDK adopters (engineers integrating Redwood into an app)
- Solutions engineers running onboarding labs
- DevEx product/engineers building onboarding flows and telemetry

High-level goals:
- Provide a 30-minute path from zero to an instrumented sample app calling Redwood (chat or embedding).
- Capture minimal telemetry events that surface readiness, errors, and cost-impacting conditions.
- Create microflow scripts for SEs to run live with customers and for internal shadowing.
- Keep each step observable and reversible.

Principles (mini):
- Keep it pragmatic: no more than 6 steps.
- Telemetry-first: design the events before the UI or README copy.
- Fail loud, recover fast: explicit fallbacks in flows.
- Reuse small artifacts: single-file examples, tiny test data, proto prompts.

Quick 30-minute microflow (concierge script) - ideal for an SE call:
1) Pre-call prep (5 min):
   - Confirm customer has an API key (create sandbox key if not).
   - Open temporary sandbox in partner org: sandbox.redwood/guest/<id>.
   - Share a single-file sample: sample-app/app.js (Node) and sample-app/README.md.
2) Local run (10 min):
   - Clone repo: git clone https://github.com/redwood-infra/sdk-concierge.git && cd sdk-concierge/sample-app
   - Install: npm ci || pip install -r requirements.txt
   - Env: export REDWOOD_API_KEY="<sandbox-key>"; export RW_ENV="sandbox"
   - Run: node app.js --mode quick || python app.py --mode quick
   - Observe a single successful response: "Hello from Redwood" (we keep the sample deterministic).
3) Instrument (8 min):
   - Toggle telemetry (ENV var RW_TELEMETRY=on). Restart.
   - Confirm telemetry stream to devexp-inbox: tail -f ./devexp/telemetry.log
   - Trigger an intentional error (bad model name) to see error event.
4) Wrap-up (7 min):
   - Show latency & token cost quick glance by reading ./devexp/summary.txt or the Console Demo route.
   - Capture next action: add embeddings, change model, or integrate into a real route.

Minimal telemetry schema (NO nested objects; kept intentionally compact for quick ingestion):
- event: string (one of: onboarding_start, sample_run_success, sample_run_error, telemetry_enabled, model_rollout_attempt, billing_threshold_crossed)
- user_id: string (anonymized session id)
- session_id: string
- step: string (which microflow step triggered the event)
- latency_ms: string (measured end-to-end request)
- tokens_in: string
- tokens_out: string
- error_code: string (optional)

Sample minimal events (line-delimited JSON in telemetry.log):
{"event":"onboarding_start","user_id":"u_2381","session_id":"s_20251104_01","step":"precall"}
{"event":"telemetry_enabled","user_id":"u_2381","session_id":"s_20251104_01","step":"instrument","latency_ms":"N/A"}
{"event":"sample_run_success","user_id":"u_2381","session_id":"s_20251104_01","step":"local_run","latency_ms":"220","tokens_in":"12","tokens_out":"58"}

Sample quickstart README (short):
- Purpose: Run a one-file demo that calls Redwood and writes telemetry locally.
- Commands (Node):
   1) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_test_xxx
   2) npm ci && node app.js --mode quick
- Commands (Python):
   1) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_test_xxx
   2) pip install -r requirements.txt && python app.py --mode quick
- Where to look: ./devexp/telemetry.log and ./devexp/summary.txt

Safety & fallback heuristics (for live demos):
- If the demo hits rate limit: set RW_FAKE_RESPONSE=1 to show deterministic fallback output.
- If latency spikes above 2s: switch to smaller model with env RW_MODEL_HINT=gpt-small-8b
- If billing threshold > $5 in sandbox: switch to token_budget=50 in sample config.

Lab recipes (short variants)
- Lab A: Embedder smoke (10 min)\   - Use sample-embed.py with a 3 sentence document set. Confirm embedding vector lengths and a single similarity query.
- Lab B: Chat + function call (20 min)\   - Use sample-chat-fn.js. Show tool-call mock and how the SDK surfaces structured output.
- Lab C: Canary rollback simulation (15 min)\   - Simulate a model regression by toggling RW_MODEL_VERSION and show auto-fallback to last-stable.

Developer outputs we should ship with the playbook:
- one-file sample apps (node, python), each < 150 LOC
- telemetry reader script (tailer) that prints human readable summary
- short SE script (bullet script for a 30-min call)
- checklist for customer handoff (email template + required envs)

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How aggressive should telemetry be by default? (privacy & cost concerns)
- Do we auto-enable telemetry in sandbox sessions? Risk: surprise data capture.
- How much of the flow should be automated vs manual for SEs? (automation reduces friction but reduces coaching opportunities)

Next steps (short):
- [ ] Iterate sample-apps to remove all non-essential deps (Arjun) - due EOD 2025-11-21
- [ ] Wire a demo Console view that reads telemetry.log and renders the 6 core events (Lena) - due 2025-12-05
- [ ] Draft SE script + slide (Samir) - due 2025-11-25
- [ ] Sync with privacy/legal on telemetry opt-in wording (Maya) - due 2025-11-28

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep prompt text in a separate file so we can A/B prompt variations without touching code.
- Consider a tiny hosted sandbox that replays sample responses to avoid real API spend during workshops.
- Use very short deterministic prompts for the 30-min path so signal is stable across networks and regions.

References & shortcuts:
- Console demo route: /demo/onramp/concierge (internal only)
- Slack channel: #devexp-onboarding (use for live-run coordination)
- GH: https://github.com/redwood-infra/sdk-concierge (sample app + CI)

End of draft.

-- Maya C. (quick notes, iterative)
